| `d8141f43` | mgr: migrate from boost::variant to std::variant | Commit_function_map lists this commit as touching the constructor. The diff hunk (`@@ -21,7`) opens at the closing `}` of the constructor (context line) but the only modification is line 24 inside `process_reports`. This is a **false positive** in commit_function_map — no constructor logic was changed. |

#### Invariants

- **INV-CTOR-1** (`f6ba1eea`): Constructor must forward the `MetricListener&` reference unchanged to the base `MetricCollector` template. No additional initialization was ever specified.
- **INV-CTOR-2** (`c2470f27`): After `c2470f27`, the class carries `struct timespec last_updated_mono` as a private member (`.h:16`, blame line 85). This member is **not initialized** in the constructor body or via a member initializer list. The C++ standard leaves POD struct members of class objects in an indeterminate state if not explicitly initialized.

#### Implementation critique

```
.cc:16-21  MDSPerfMetricCollector::MDSPerfMetricCollector(MetricListener &listener)
.cc:17-20    : MetricCollector<...>(listener) {
.cc:21     }

The constructor at `.cc:16-21` has an empty body with no member initializer for `last_updated_mono`. Any call to `get_last_updated()` before the first `process_reports()` will read uninitialized memory and produce a garbage timestamp. The commit that introduced `last_updated_mono` did not add `last_updated_mono{}` to the constructor MIL.

### 2. `__anon532cff820102` (anonymous lambda)

**Location**: `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.cc:28`

> This is the counter-update lambda passed to `process_reports_generic` inside `process_reports`. ctags identifies it as a distinct syntactic entity.

#### Commit history

| SHA | Subject | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `f6ba1eea` | mds: forward mds metrics to ceph manager | Created lambda. Signature: `[](PerformanceCounter *counter, const PerformanceCounter &update)`. Body: `counter->first = update.first; counter->second = update.second;` |

#### Invariants

- **INV-LAMBDA-1** (`f6ba1eea`): The counter update strategy is **absolute replacement**, not delta accumulation. `counter->first` and `counter->second` are overwritten unconditionally with incoming values. This distinguishes MDS counter semantics from OSD-style counters that accumulate deltas.
- **INV-LAMBDA-2** (`f6ba1eea`): The lambda is stateless (no captures). `process_reports_generic` owns the locking; the lambda only performs the atomic field assignment.

#### Implementation critique

```
.cc:28  metric_report.reports, [](PerformanceCounter *counter, const PerformanceCounter &update) {
.cc:29    counter->first = update.first;
.cc:30    counter->second = update.second;
.cc:31  });
```

- **OK**: Implementation matches the established contract exactly.
- **UNGROUNDED**: No comment explains why this uses absolute replacement rather than accumulation. The intent is inferred from the single creation commit (`f6ba1eea`) with no subsequent revision. A reader cannot tell from the code alone whether this is intentional or an unfinished delta-tracking design.

### 3. `process_reports`

**Location**: `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.cc:23`, declared `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.h:24`

#### Commit history

| SHA | Subject | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `f6ba1eea` | mds: forward mds metrics to ceph manager | Created. Extracts `MDSPerfMetricReport` from `boost::get<MDSMetricPayload>(payload)`, acquires lock, calls `process_reports_generic` with the replacement lambda, updates `delayed_ranks`, logs at dout(20). |
| `d8141f43` | mgr: migrate from boost::variant to std::variant | `.cc:24`: `boost::get<MDSMetricPayload>(payload)` → `std::get<MDSMetricPayload>(payload)`. Pure mechanical substitution; no semantic change. |
| `c2470f27` | mgr, pybind/mgr, mgr/stats: be resilient to offline rank0 MDS | `.cc:36-37`: Added blank line + `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE, &last_updated_mono)` after the `delayed_ranks` update. Establishes the "timestamp every report batch" invariant. |

#### Invariants

- **INV-PR-1** (`f6ba1eea`): The payload **must** be of type `MDSMetricPayload`. `std::get<>` throws `std::bad_variant_access` for any other type. No try/catch is present and none was ever added — callers are required to route only MDS payloads to this instance.
- **INV-PR-2** (`f6ba1eea`): Lock (`lock`) must be acquired **before** `process_reports_generic` is called and **before** `delayed_ranks` is written. The variant extraction at `.cc:24` happens outside the lock — this is intentional since the payload reference is read-only.
- **INV-PR-3** (`f6ba1eea`): `delayed_ranks` is updated in every call, even when the report set is empty.
- **INV-PR-4** (`c2470f27`): `last_updated_mono` is captured via `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE, ...)` **after** all data mutations (generic report processing + delayed_ranks update). The timestamp reflects the wall-clock moment the complete batch was applied.

#### Implementation critique

```
.cc:23  void MDSPerfMetricCollector::process_reports(const MetricPayload &payload) {
.cc:24    const MDSPerfMetricReport &metric_report = std::get<MDSMetricPayload>(payload).metric_report;
.cc:25
.cc:26    std::lock_guard locker(lock);
.cc:27    process_reports_generic(
.cc:28      metric_report.reports, [](PerformanceCounter *counter, const PerformanceCounter &update) {
.cc:29        counter->first = update.first;
.cc:30        counter->second = update.second;
.cc:31      });
.cc:32
.cc:33    // update delayed rank set
.cc:34    delayed_ranks = metric_report.rank_metrics_delayed;
.cc:35    dout(20) << ": delayed ranks=[" << delayed_ranks << "]" << dendl;
.cc:36
.cc:37    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE, &last_updated_mono);
.cc:38  }
```

- **OK**: `std::get<>` at line 24 correctly replaces `boost::get<>` per `d8141f43`.
- **OK**: `clock_gettime` call at line 37 correctly implements INV-PR-4 per `c2470f27`.
- **UNGROUNDED (line 24)**: The variant extraction is performed **outside** the lock. This is safe only if `payload` is immutable during `process_reports`. No documentation or assertion enforces this. If any concurrent path could modify the payload between line 24 and line 26, there is a data race. In practice, payloads are call-stack-owned, but this is not asserted.
- **UNGROUNDED (line 37)**: `CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE` is used rather than `CLOCK_MONOTONIC`. The coarse clock has lower resolution (~10ms on Linux). No comment explains why low-resolution is acceptable for MDS failover detection (the use case from `c2470f27`'s fix for tracker issue #50033).

### 4. `get_counters`

**Location**: `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.cc:40`, declared `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.h:25`

#### Commit history

| `c2470f27` | mgr, pybind/mgr, mgr/stats: be resilient to offline rank0 MDS | `.cc:52`: Inserted `get_last_updated(&c->last_updated_mono)` between `get_delayed_ranks` and `return r`. |

#### Invariants

- **INV-GC-1** (`7523aef6`): `collector` is always an `MDSPerfCollector*`. The `static_cast` is unchecked — callers must not pass any other `PerfCollector` subtype.
- **INV-GC-2** (`7523aef6`): `get_delayed_ranks` is called only when `get_counters_generic` succeeds (`r == 0`). If the query is unknown/invalid, `delayed_ranks` is NOT populated in the output collector.
- **INV-GC-3** (`c2470f27`): `get_last_updated` follows the same conditionality as `get_delayed_ranks` — only called on success. The timestamp is written to `c->last_updated_mono` under lock.
- **INV-GC-4** (`7523aef6`): The function holds `lock` for the entire duration including `get_delayed_ranks` and `get_last_updated`, ensuring `delayed_ranks` and `last_updated_mono` are read atomically with the counters snapshot.

#### Implementation critique

```
.cc:40  int MDSPerfMetricCollector::get_counters(PerfCollector *collector) {
.cc:41    MDSPerfCollector *c = static_cast<MDSPerfCollector *>(collector);
.cc:42
.cc:43    std::lock_guard locker(lock);
.cc:44
.cc:45    int r = get_counters_generic(c->query_id, &c->counters);
.cc:46    if (r != 0) {
.cc:47      return r;
.cc:48    }
.cc:49
.cc:50    get_delayed_ranks(&c->delayed_ranks);
.cc:51
.cc:52    get_last_updated(&c->last_updated_mono);
.cc:53    return r;
.cc:54  }
```

- **OK**: Implementation matches all invariants established by `7523aef6` and `c2470f27`.
- **UNGROUNDED (line 41)**: `static_cast` is unguarded. No `dynamic_cast`-check or assertion that `collector` is non-null. History never added a null-check, and `f6ba1eea`/`7523aef6` provide no rationale. This is consistent with the pattern in the broader codebase (PerfCollector callers own lifetime), but the invariant is implicit.
- **UNGROUNDED (lines 46-48)**: The early return on `r != 0` leaves `c->delayed_ranks` and `c->last_updated_mono` in whatever state they were before the call (potentially uninitialized if this is the first call). No commit has ever documented what the caller should expect in the error path.

**Location**: `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.cc:61`, declared `src/mgr/MDSPerfMetricCollector.h:20`

#### Commit history

| SHA | Subject | What changed |
|---|---|---|

Added `struct timespec last_updated_mono` member to class (`.h:16`), added `get_last_updated(utime_t *ts)` declaration (`.h:20`), added `clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_COARSE, &last_updated_mono)` call in `process_reports` (`.cc:37`), added `get_last_updated(&c->last_updated_mono)` in `get_counters` (`.cc:52`), added implementation (`.cc:61-64`). Motivation: fix tracker issue #50033 — enable `ceph fs perf stats` to detect MDS rank0 failover by exposing when metrics were last updated. |

#### Invariants

- **INV-GLU-1** (`c2470f27`): Caller must hold `lock`. Enforced by `ceph_assert(ceph_mutex_is_locked(lock))`.
- **INV-GLU-2** (`c2470f27`): Output is `utime_t` converted from `struct timespec` (monotonic clock). The conversion via `utime_t(last_updated_mono)` implies a `utime_t` constructor from `timespec` exists.
- **INV-GLU-3** (`c2470f27`): The timestamp is **only valid** after at least one `process_reports()` call. Before the first call, `last_updated_mono` is uninitialized (see DIVERGED in constructor section).

#### Implementation critique

```
.cc:61  void MDSPerfMetricCollector::get_last_updated(utime_t *ts) {
.cc:62    ceph_assert(ceph_mutex_is_locked(lock));
.cc:63    *ts = utime_t(last_updated_mono);
.cc:64  }
```

- **DIVERGED** (`c2470f27`): INV-GLU-3 is not enforced. `c2470f27` established that `last_updated_mono` is set by `process_reports` but did not add an assertion or sentinel to guard the pre-first-call state. The constructor does not zero-initialize `last_updated_mono`, so any call to `get_last_updated` (directly or via `get_counters`) before the first `process_reports` returns an indeterminate `utime_t`. The commit that created this function (`c2470f27`) is the one that should have added `last_updated_mono{}` to the constructor MIL.
- **UNGROUNDED (line 63)**: The `utime_t(timespec)` constructor contract is not visible here. If `utime_t` performs signed arithmetic on `tv_sec`/`tv_nsec`, a zero-initialized (but never-set) `last_updated_mono` would yield epoch time, which could silently look valid to callers rather than flagging an uninitialized state.

## Cross-Cutting Analysis

### Locking discipline

All mutable state (`delayed_ranks`, `last_updated_mono`) is protected by `lock` (inherited from `MetricCollector`). The pattern is consistent:
- Writers (`process_reports`): `std::lock_guard` at `.cc:26`, acquired **after** the variant extraction.
- Readers (`get_delayed_ranks`, `get_last_updated`): `ceph_assert(ceph_mutex_is_locked(lock))` — callee asserts, not caller-provided guard. The only public read path (`get_counters`) acquires the lock before calling either.

No locking gaps identified in the current implementation. The variant extraction at `.cc:24` outside the lock is safe given read-only payload semantics but is UNGROUNDED (no comment or assertion).

### Variant type safety

`f6ba1eea` used `boost::get<>` (throws `boost::bad_get` on wrong type). `d8141f4` migrated to `std::get<>` (throws `std::bad_variant_access`). Both propagate type mismatches as exceptions. The migration is complete and consistent — no `boost::get` remains.

### Uninitialized member (`last_updated_mono`)

The most significant finding. Summary of evidence:
- `c2470f27` added `struct timespec last_updated_mono` to the class header (`.h:16`).
- `c2470f27` added no member initializer in the constructor.
- `f6ba1eea` established the constructor with an empty body and an MIL that only invokes the base.
- No subsequent commit has added initialization.
- `get_last_updated` reads this field without a validity guard.

**Recommended fix** (not applied — read-only assessment): Add `last_updated_mono{}` to the constructor MIL, or add a sentinel (e.g., `last_updated_mono.tv_sec == 0 && last_updated_mono.tv_nsec == 0` check) inside `get_last_updated`.
